title: Committee of Supply – Head Q (Ministry of Communications and Information)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head Q (Ministry of Communications and Information)

sections.label: Vibrant economy and business growth
sections.summary: A vibrant economy driven by competitive companies, skilled employees and efficient infrastructure underpins higher wages for workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: One of the basic building blocks of a strong nation is a vibrant economy, an economy that is driven by competitive companies with skilled and creative employees and underpinned by an efficient infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Strong business and productivity growth are preconditions for higher wages for our workers.

sections.label: Older workers in workforce
sections.summary: One in four of the workforce is aged 55 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Today, one in four of our workforce is aged 55 and above.

sections.label: Government digitalisation interoperability standards
sections.summary: The Government can set interoperability standards to help a reliable, resilient, accessible and secure local digital infrastructure ecosystem thrive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: To accelerate the pace of digitalisation, the Government can set interoperability standards so that a local ecosystem of digital infrastructure that is reliable, resilient, accessible and secure can take root and thrive.

sections.label: Plans to help businesses innovate
sections.summary: The question asks the Minister to lay out plans to help large and small businesses adopt technology and innovate in the digital economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Could the Minister lay out for this House his plans to assist our businesses, both large and small, to adopt technology and to innovate in this digital economy?

sections.label: SkillsFuture, Adapt and Grow training
sections.summary: SkillsFuture and Adapt and Grow are cited as examples, and businesses must step up training and job redesign through professional conversion programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
sentences.text: The SkillsFuture and Adapt and Grow programmes are some good examples.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
sentences.text: Businesses, too, must step up on training and job redesign through professional conversion programmes for employees.

sections.label: ASEAN digital economy and e-payments
sections.summary: Bain & Co research says harnessing the region's digital economies could add US$1 trillion to ASEAN GDP by 2025, with a common e-payment platform facilitating this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, according to research by Bain & Co, harnessing the collective power potential of the region's digital economies could accelerate intraregional trade and result in a gross domestic product uplift of US$1 trillion across the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
sentences.text: For example, a common e-payment platform would facilitate the ASEAN digital economy, to ensure interoperability across state boundaries and leverage the large ASEAN market for e-commerce.

sections.label: ASEAN secure cyberspace framework
sections.summary: ASEAN needs to develop a secure cyberspace by building and reinforcing the framework for online security to minimise cyber threat risks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
sentences.text: To minimise the risks of cyber threats, ASEAN needs to develop a secure cyberspace through building and reinforcing the framework for online security.

sections.label: SMEs going digital uptake
sections.summary: It asks whether more companies are coming forward, noting there are almost 200,000 SMEs in Singapore and questioning how many have gone digital.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: And are we really seeing more and more companies coming forward?

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: There are almost 200,000 SMEs around in Singapore but how many have taken up and gone digital?

sections.label: Switzerland future of work skills
sections.summary: An October 2018 McKinsey report estimates declining demand for basic cognitive and physical skills and rising demand for social, emotional and technological skills in Switzerland.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: According to an October 2018 McKinsey report on the future of work in Switzerland, it is estimated that the demand for tasks requiring basic cognitive or physical and manual skills could decline by 20%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Conversely, the need for social and emotional and technological skills is to rise by about 20% and up to 50% respectively.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The skill shift is also expected to exceed the regular rate at which labour and skills drop out of the market.

sections.label: ICT career switch programmes
sections.summary: It asks whether programmes exist to help individuals with no Infocomm technology background make the career switch.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: For individuals with no Infocomm technology (ICT) background, are there programmes in place to help them make the career switch?

sections.label: SMEs adopting pre-approved digital solutions
sections.summary: Finance Minister Heng Swee Keat announced in Budget 2019 that about 4,000 SMEs adopted pre-approved digital solutions, a small share of nearly 200,000 SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As announced by Finance Minister Heng Swee Keat in Budget 2019, the programme has seen some 4,000 SMEs adopt pre-approved digital solutions offered under the programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While this number is indeed encouraging, it is a drop in an ocean of nearly 200,000 SMEs in Singapore.

sections.label: ICM Industry Transformation Map goals
sections.summary: The ICM Industry Transformation Map, launched in November 2017, aimed to employ over 210,000 ICM workers and create over 13,000 PMET jobs by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The ICM Industry Transformation Map (ITM) was launched in November 2017 with the goal of employing more than 210,000 ICM workers and create more than 13,000 professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMET) jobs by 2020.

sections.label: PDPC fines SingHealth and IHiS
sections.summary: The PDPC fined SingHealth S$250,000 and IHiS S$750,000, signalling other organisations to safeguard personal data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On 15 January 2019, the Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC) fined SingHealth S$250,000 and fined the Integrated Health Information Systems Pte Ltd (IHiS) S$750,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These punitive fines underscore the large scale of the breach and the sensitive and confidential nature of the patients' data that was lost and it is a signal to other organisations to take the necessary steps to safeguard personal data.

sections.label: PDPC enquiries and complaints classes
sections.summary: PDPC received between 2,200 and 3,300 enquiries and complaints annually over four years, and the question asks which classes were major.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the PDPC's website, the number of enquiries and complaints received by it in the last four years ranged from between 2,200 and 3,300 annually.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: First, were the major classes of complaints related to the "Do Not Call" Registry or were they complaints about organisations not exercising reasonable care to protect personal data from unauthorised disclosure?

sections.label: PDPC redress and public agencies exclusion
sections.summary: The passage asks whether PDPC has assisted breach victims with redress and whether there is reason to exclude public agencies from PDPA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Has PDPC ever assisted a victim of a data breach to obtain redress, for example, mediating a financial settlement with the organisation?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While I accept that Government agencies have many laws and regulations concerning data obligations, is there a convincing reason to exclude public agencies from PDPA?

sections.label: Government and AI societal concerns
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government has considered societal concerns about AI use and how they are addressed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Has the Government considered societal concerns surrounding the use of AI and, if so, how are we addressing them?

sections.label: Budget 2019 Digital Defence pillar
sections.summary: Budget 2019 added the Digital Defence pillar to Singapore's Total Defence strategy, focusing attention on cybersecurity.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Chairman, Budget 2019 has focused our attention on cybersecurity by adding the Digital Defence pillar to our Total Defence strategy.

sections.label: Cybersecurity initiatives for businesses and SMEs
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government will consider targeted initiatives to bolster cybersecurity capabilities of businesses, especially local SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In Singapore, the extensive interface between the private and public sectors means that cybersecurity for businesses is a critical vulnerability.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Will the Government thus consider implementing targeted initiatives to bolster the cybersecurity capabilities of businesses, especially our local SMEs, urgently?

sections.label: SingHealth and MOH data breaches
sections.summary: Two incidents are cited: unauthorised access of SingHealth records by a foreign state actor and improper leak of MOH's AIDS patient registry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: The first was the unauthorised access of SingHealth records by a foreign state actor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: The second involved the improper leak of the Ministry of Health's (MOH's) registry of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS) patients.

sections.label: Singapore crime and cyberattack trends
sections.summary: Overall crime rose 1.4% on online scams, Computer Misuse Act crimes rose 40.3%, and the SingHealth cyberattack affected 1.5 million patients.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Last year, Singapore's overall crime rate went up by 1.4%, propped up mainly by a surge in online-related scams.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: There was also a 40.3% increase in the number of crimes under the Computer Misuse Act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: We have also seen several instances of cyberattacks in public domains, like the recent high-profile SingHealth cyberattack which affected 1.5 million patients.

sections.label: Digital Defence and human weakness
sections.summary: With Digital Defence as Total Defence's sixth pillar, humans or computer users are in most cases the weakest link in cybersecurity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: As we introduce Digital Defence as the sixth pillar of Total Defence in Singapore, we must remember that in most cases, humans or computer users are the weakest link in cybersecurity.

sections.label: COI cybersecurity personnel competency
sections.summary: The COI investigating the SingHealth cyberattack recommended significantly improving the competency of cybersecurity personnel.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Sir, the COI investigating the SingHealth cyberattack recommended to significantly improve the competency of cybersecurity personnel.

sections.label: Key issues on fake news
sections.summary: Five issues on fake news are listed, and the question asks whether new measures will counter deliberate online falsehoods as recommended.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: Some of the key issues raised included: first, fake news is often plausible and interesting, which makes it likely to circulate very far; second, the truth is rarely as interesting, so corrections and rectifications do not get the same attention; third, social media and messaging platforms, such as WhatsApp, have allowed fake news to go very far; fourth, there is evidence that foreign actors have used fake news to interfere in elections, such as the US Presidential election and even the United Kingdom's (UK's) vote on Brexit; fifth, private organisations often profit from fake news, and these include not only those who deliberately create it, such as Temasek Review, but many of those who benefit from its dissemination, including platforms like Facebook which get monies from advertising revenues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: After the Select Committee's deliberation, are there any plans to introduce new measures to counter the threat of deliberate online falsehoods as recommended by the Select Committee?

sections.label: Basic Digital Skills Curriculum questions
sections.summary: Questions ask how the Basic Digital Skills Curriculum maps against Internet usage trends and what plans refresh it for technological and workplace changes.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun
sentences.text: How do we then map the skills covered by the Basic Digital Skills Curriculum against prevailing Internet usage trends in Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun
sentences.text: Also, what plans are in place to have the curriculum regularly refreshed to take into account (a) shifting technological trends and (b) changing needs in schools and workplaces?

sections.label: Bridging the digital divide
sections.summary: The Member asks the Minister for strategies and plans to bridge the digital divide so everyone can benefit from the digital economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng
sentences.text: Given the numerous impediments to digital inclusion, I would like to ask the Minister to share his strategies and plans to bridge the digital divide so that everyone can benefit from the digital economy.

sections.label: MacPherson survey and digital help
sections.summary: A MacPherson survey of 315 public rental residents found know-how, smartphones and data plans were the largest barriers, and the Member asks what the Ministry has done for seniors and the digitally vulnerable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: In MacPherson, we conducted a simple survey of 315 public rental residents last year and identified that the largest barriers with going digital are know-how, possession of smartphones and data plans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: With the ability of oversight and access to a much larger network of resources, I would like to ask the Ministry what has been done to target efforts at helping seniors and the digitally vulnerable to learn, access and use digital technologies to enhance their quality of life?

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Sir, our libraries are a wonderful resource to instil knowledge in our people.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin
sentences.text: I understand that there have been collaborative efforts between the National Library Board (NLB) and SkillsFuture Singapore to upgrade the skills of Singaporeans.

sections.label: Data-sharing platform proposal
sections.summary: The Member suggests creating a data-sharing platform between SkillsFuture Singapore and the National Library Board.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin
sentences.text: In fact, we can go one step further and create a data-sharing platform between SkillsFuture Singapore and NLB.

sections.label: Libraries as inclusive social space
sections.summary: The Member asks how the Government ensures libraries remain an inclusive social space for Singaporeans of all ages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: How does the Government ensure that our libraries continue to serve as an inclusive social space for Singaporeans of all ages?

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 3.20 pm.

sections.label: Government survey statistics reply
sections.summary: The Member recalls Minister Yaacob Ibrahim replying that the Government does not compile statistics on surveys by various agencies or which are published, and says published survey results would be valuable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In a reply to my previous Parliamentary Question, then Minister Yaacob Ibrahim responded that "The Government does not compile statistics on the surveys conducted by various agencies, or which among them are published." The results of opinion surveys, if published, would be valuable to many stakeholders in society.

sections.label: Publishing surveys and government efficiency
sections.summary: The Member states that publishing such surveys could improve governmental efficiency and spending by reducing survey overlaps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If not, the publication of such surveys could even improve governmental efficiency and spending by reducing survey overlaps.

sections.label: Government policy communications across groups
sections.summary: An MP asks the Ministry how it intends to improve communication of Government policies across age groups and communities to maximise policy impact.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Given the imperative of effective policy communications, I would like to ask the Ministry how it intends to improve the communication of Government policies across different age groups and communities to maximise policy impact and benefit the intended audience?

sections.label: PSB in changing media landscape
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Government can share how PSB is changing in the evolving media landscape.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: Can the Government share how PSB is changing in this ever-evolving media landscape?

sections.label: Growing media industry domestically and overseas
sections.summary: The question asks about general plans to develop the media industry domestically and whether local media firms will be supported overseas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David
sentences.text: What are our general plans to develop/grow the media industry domestically and are there plans to support local media firms overseas?

sections.label: SMEs benefiting from digital programme
sections.summary: About 4,000 SMEs have benefited from a programme providing step-by-step guides to go digital.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: To date, about 4,000 SMEs have benefited from this programme, which provides access to step-by-step guides to go digital.

sections.label: Start Digital Pack with partners
sections.summary: Working with banks and telco partners, the Start Digital Pack was launched in January this year for companies from establishment.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: For instance, working with banks and telco partners, we launched the Start Digital Pack in January this year, so that digital solutions can be adopted by companies from the moment they are established.

sections.label: AI and cloud solutions for sectors
sections.summary: A pre-approved cloud-based AI solution increased deliveries by 20% and revenue by 15%, and by 2020 AI- and cloud-based solutions will roll out to every sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: They use a pre-approved cloud-based AI solution to optimise delivery routes and dynamically reassign drivers to new routes based on the capacity and locations of available vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: This has enabled them to increase their deliveries by 20% and revenue by 15%.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: By 2020, we will roll out AI- and cloud-based solutions to every sector so that more businesses can benefit.

sections.label: ICT training places taken up
sections.summary: Over 61,000 training places have been taken up or committed, about a third of the total ICT workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Since then, over 61,000 training places have been taken up or committed, which accounts for about a third, slightly more, of our total ICT workforce.

sections.label: Wan Ru IoT Engineer outcome
sections.summary: Wan Ru learnt IoT skills and is now an IoT Engineer, and 90% of beneficiaries remain in ICT roles.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Through the programme, Wan Ru learnt skills in the Internet-of Things (IoT) domain and is now an IoT Engineer.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, we have seen good results from these programmes and I would like to inform Ms Tin Pei Ling that 90% of the beneficiaries continue to be in ICT roles.

sections.label: SDE research funding allocation
sections.summary: A further $300 million will be allocated for research in the SDE domain, almost doubling the current budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: We must sustain this research and innovation momentum that underpins our Digital Economy strategies.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: I am, therefore, pleased to announce and share with Members that we will allocate a further $300 million for research in the SDE domain, almost doubling it from the current budget.

sections.label: PDPC complaints in 2018
sections.summary: In 2018, the PDPC processed 1,669 data protection complaints and 1,236 Do Not Call complaints.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: To Ms Sylvia Lim's query, in 2018, the PDPC processed 1,669 complaints on data protection issues and 1,236 on Do Not Call issues.

sections.label: PDPA and PSGA standards aligned
sections.summary: Data protection standards in the PDPA and PSGA are broadly aligned, with public agencies subject to the same or higher standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The data protection standards in PDPA and the Public Sector Governance Act (PSGA) are broadly aligned.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Public agencies are subject to the same, if not higher standards, than the private sector.

sections.label: Model AI Governance Framework launch
sections.summary: Singapore's Model AI Governance Framework was launched to guide private organisations in deploying AI safely and ethically.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Mr Vikram Nair asked about AI ethics, which is an area we are focused on, given the pervasive potential of AI technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And to this end, I recently launched Singapore's Model AI Governance Framework to guide private organisations, in particular, to deploy AI solutions safely and ethically.

sections.label: 5G rollout and consultation
sections.summary: Singapore plans to start 5G rollout by 2020, with IMDA launching a public consultation on regulatory framework and spectrum allocation.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: To Mr Ong Teng Koon's query on infrastructure, we aim to ensure that we have future-ready and globally competitive digital infrastructure which is the bedrock of our digital economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, we plan to commence the rollout of fifth generation mobile networks, or what is more commonly known as 5G, by 2020 to maintain Singapore's competitive edge in connectivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: With 5G, businesses and citizens can experience peak data rates of up to 100 times faster than 4G, with up to 25 times lower latency, and the ability to support up to 1,000 times more devices per square kilometre.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: IMDA will launch a public consultation shortly to help us develop the right regulatory framework and policies for 5G, including the allocation of spectrum.

sections.label: Digital Clinics and Singapore Fund
sections.summary: Digital Clinics reached over 4,000 individuals since 2017, and Our Singapore Fund will support digital readiness community efforts with MCCY.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Our Digital Clinics have reached more than 4,000 individuals since 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And this was only possible with the support of 20 corporate partners and 1,000 volunteers like Ms Poh.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: To support many more Singaporeans like Ms Poh who are passionate about helping others, we will launch Our Singapore Fund, which will support community efforts that promote digital readiness.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: This is in collaboration with the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY), and Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary will be elaborating on these initiatives.

sections.label: Shared digital economy endeavour
sections.summary: Building a vibrant digital economy is a shared endeavour, with challenges faced by individuals, workers and smaller enterprises addressed through collaboration.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, if I may conclude, the building of a vibrant digital economy in Singapore is a shared endeavour.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And the video we have just seen highlights that there are challenges, whether we are individuals, workers or smaller enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In different ways, we are dealing with these challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And it also shows how we can collaborate and succeed.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, let us work together, as digitally-empowered businesses, digitally-skilled workers and digitally-connected citizens to realise that vision.

sections.label: Digital Readiness Blueprint and Council
sections.summary: Last year, the Digital Readiness Blueprint was launched and a Digital Readiness Council was set up.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Last year, we launched the Digital Readiness Blueprint and set up a Digital Readiness Council.

sections.label: Digital Participation Pledge organisations
sections.summary: The voluntary Digital Participation Pledge has 270 organisations, with a target of 3,000 organisations by 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: The Digital Participation Pledge, which the Minister announced, is a voluntary, online pledge, to encourage organisations to promote digital participation and inclusion.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: And already, 270 organisations from a wide range of industries – not just the tech industry, not just the online industry, but any industry that can make use of these digital technologies – have done so and pledged their commitment to expand their digital readiness efforts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Our target is to have 3,000 organisations on board this Pledge by 2021.

sections.label: Project funding amounts
sections.summary: Projects can receive up to $20,000 of funding, to support up to 80% of project costs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Projects can receive up to $20,000 of funding, to support up to 80% of project costs.

sections.label: Silver Infocomm Initiatives reach seniors
sections.summary: The Silver Infocomm Initiatives have collectively reached over 270,000 seniors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Collectively, our Silver Infocomm Initiatives have reached over 270,000 seniors.

sections.label: Information and media literacy framework
sections.summary: An information and media literacy framework is being developed, with desired outcomes and content guidelines, to be rolled out later this year and refreshed regularly.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: In the longer term, we are also developing an information and media literacy framework that pools together relevant information, media and cyber literacy skills that Singaporeans need to use social media and digital technology responsibly and safely.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: This framework will spell out a set of desired outcomes and include content guidelines for programme owners to reference.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We aim to roll it out later this year and to refresh it regularly.

sections.label: Government Bug Bounty Programme results
sections.summary: From December last year to January, 400 white hat hackers took part in the Government Bug Bounty Programme and identified 26 vulnerabilities in five Government systems, all remediated.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: From December last year to January, 400 "white hat" hackers – "white hat" hackers are people who have hacking skills and use them for good, as compared to "black hat" hackers who do so for criminal reasons – took part in the Government Bug Bounty Programme organised by Government Technology Agency (GovTech) and CSA.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: They have “stress-tested” the defences of five Internet-facing Government systems and identified 26 vulnerabilities, all of which have been remediated.

sections.label: Cyber Security Innovation and Growth Programme
sections.summary: In 2019 the Government will expand the Call for Innovation into the Cyber Security Innovation and Growth Programme to support local cybersecurity companies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: In 2019, the Government will expand the Call for Innovation into the Cyber Security Innovation and Growth Programme to support local cybersecurity companies to create innovative and relevant cybersecurity solutions and to meet the changing needs of the industry.

sections.label: Cybersecurity jobs tripled
sections.summary: The total number of cybersecurity professional jobs across public and private sectors tripled from 2012 to 2017, to 5,300.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Across the public and private sectors, the total number of jobs for cybersecurity professionals tripled from 2012 to 2017, to 5,300.

sections.label: Companies to develop cybersecurity professionals
sections.summary: Eight companies have committed to develop more than 900 professionals by 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Eight companies have committed to develop more than 900 professionals by 2021.

sections.label: Singapore cybersecurity standards regime
sections.summary: MCI's work on cybersecurity standards led to Singapore becoming a Common Criteria Certificate Authorising Nation in January 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: As part of MCI's work to ensure our standards and regulations support the growth of the digital economy, we have made progress in building a strong cybersecurity standards regime in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: I am pleased to announce that this has resulted in Singapore attaining the status of a Common Criteria Certificate Authorising Nation as of January 2019.

sections.label: Authorising Nation benefits local companies
sections.summary: As an Authorising Nation, Singapore lets local companies develop globally recognised products locally, saving cost and time.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: There is an ecosystem of 30 countries that recognise this, but we have now attained the status of an Authorising Nation, to produce the products and extend it globally.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: This will allow local companies to develop globally recognised products within Singapore, with estimated cost and time savings, because you do not have to send your product overseas for evaluation, nor bring the testers and evaluators here to Singapore.

sections.label: Revamped libraries loans and visitorship
sections.summary: Revamped libraries generated 50% higher loans and about 65% more visitors than non-revamped counterparts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Our libraries of the future have been well-received by Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: They have generated 50% higher loans and an increase of around 65% in visitorship, compared with their non-revamped counterparts.

sections.label: eBook loans and quota increase
sections.summary: eBook loans more than doubled since 2017, and NLB raised the eBook loan quota from eight to 16.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Our eBook loans have more than doubled since 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: To meet the rising demand for eBooks, NLB had raised the eBook loan quota from eight to 16.

sections.label: Physical loan quota doubled
sections.summary: From 1 April the physical loan quota doubles from eight to 16 items permanently, allowing 32 physical and electronic items at one time.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: From 1 April, we will be doubling the physical loan quota from eight to 16 items permanently.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In effect, library users will be able to borrow 32 physical and electronic items at any one time.

sections.label: Workshops target over five years
sections.summary: Over the next five years, the target is 1,500 workshops benefiting more than 50,000 participants.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Over the next five years, we target to run 1,500 workshops benefiting more than 50,000 participants.

sections.label: NLB ARC special needs employment
sections.summary: NLB extends its employment partnership with the Autism Resource Centre in 2019, with ARC clients employed since January 2019 at the Lee Kong Chian Reference Library.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: To enable job creation for persons with special needs, NLB will be extending its employment partnership with the Autism Resource Centre (ARC) in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: ARC clients were trained on collection arrangement work in late 2018 and, since January 2019, they have been employed by NLB to support the operations of the Lee Kong Chian Reference Library.

sections.label: NLB loan quota increase
sections.summary: After raising the e-book loan quota to 16 in 2018, NLB will raise the physical book loan quota to 16 from April this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: In 2018, NLB increased the loan quota for e-books from eight to 16, and this was well-received by the public.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: From April this year, NLB will increase the loan quota for physical books to 16 as well.

sections.label: Adapt and Grow campaign research
sections.summary: Post-campaign research showed about eight in 10 respondents were keener to sign up for Adapt and Grow initiatives after watching the programme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Our post-campaign research showed about eight in 10 respondents were keener to sign up for Adapt and Grow initiatives after watching the programme, suggesting its effectiveness.

sections.label: Pioneer and Merdeka Generation communications
sections.summary: Surveys after the 2014 Pioneer Generation Package led to using Chinese dialects, and a similar process will plan Merdeka Generation Package communications.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: For example, after the Pioneer Generation Package was introduced in 2014, we conducted surveys to ascertain how well understood the package was by the target audience, that is, the Pioneers themselves.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: As a result of these studies, we decided to use Chinese dialects to communicate the package to our Pioneers who are less comfortable with English or Mandarin.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We will undertake a similar process in planning our communications on the Merdeka Generation Package.

sections.label: Global and Southeast Asia media growth
sections.summary: The global entertainment and media industry is expected to grow 4.4% from 2017 to 2022, with Southeast Asia's media sector growing over 7%.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The global entertainment and media industry is expected to grow by 4.4% from 2017 to 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Within Southeast Asia, the media sector is likely to grow by more than 7%.

sections.label: iPrep scheme for media students
sections.summary: The iPrep scheme will be extended to tertiary media students, providing up to $8,500 per student for industry courses, overseas internships or immersion programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: First, we will extend the iPrep scheme to media students in tertiary schools so that they can be better prepared for the rigours of the media industry when they graduate. iPrep will provide up to $8,500 per student to cover the costs of attending industry courses, overseas internships or immersion programmes.

sections.label: Festival media professionals deals
sections.summary: The Festival attracted over 23,000 media professionals and facilitated more than US$313 million worth of deals.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Last December, the Festival attracted over 23,000 media professionals and industry thought leaders and facilitated more than US$313 million worth of deals.

sections.label: Digital Archive Singapore Malay Theatre
sections.summary: Malay theatre practitioners will partner NLB to create a Digital Archive of Singapore Malay Theatre, publicly available from December this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Theatre practitioners from the Malay community will partner NLB to create a Digital Archive of Singapore Malay Theatre.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: These new databases will be a rich resource of our arts and cultural heritage, and they will be publicly available from December this year.

sections.label: Community Oral History Committees volunteers
sections.summary: Community Oral History Committees had more than 100 volunteers document over 160 hours of interviews for the national oral history collection.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Our Community Oral History Committees, representing the Malay, Chinese, Indian and Eurasian communities in Singapore, have had more than 100 volunteers document over 160 hours of interviews for our national oral history collection.

sections.label: National Archives Building Canning Rise
sections.summary: The revamped National Archives Building opens next month with three oral history recording studios and the Oldham Theatre accessible to the public.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: When the revamped National Archives Building at Canning Rise opens next month, I hope Ms Sushma and many other potential archivists will make good use of its new facilities, such as the three new oral history recording studios in the building.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The Oldham Theatre in the National Archives of Singapore (NAS) building will become accessible to members of the public, featuring regular screenings of curated films by the Asian Films Archive.

sections.label: Training courses for seniors
sections.summary: Training courses and programmes such as IMDA's Silver Info-comm Junction were set up at more than 30 locations, with mobile digital clinics for seniors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: Here, I would like to take the opportunity to introduce a few specific training courses and programmes, such as IMDA's Silver Info-comm Junction.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: These have been set up at more than 30 locations, many of them are in our community centres and some are in the libraries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: At the same time, IMDA also provides a Basic Digital Skills Curriculum working with partners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We have also set up mobile digital clinics to provide one-on-one instruction for senior citizens at different locations and time slots.

sections.label: Digital and physical library loans
sections.summary: From 2017 to 2018 digital loans almost quadrupled to 5.8 million, still a fraction of about 33 million physical loans in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: From 2017 to 2018, the digital loans have almost quadrupled from 1.5 million such loans to 5.8 million loans in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: However, this remains a fraction when compared to the physical loans, which in 2018, stood at about 33 million.

sections.label: Archives digitalisation and propagation
sections.summary: The Archives hold rich information, and this year content is being digitalised and propagated to the larger population.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In fact, the Archives have a very rich treasure trove of information.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And one of the things that we are doing in the course of this year, as I highlighted, is digitalising the content and then finding ways to propagate it with the larger population.

sections.label: Concerns about survey topics
sections.summary: The Member's reasons are concerns because some surveys may touch on security or affect market sentiments on specific sectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: As for the kind of reasons that the Member has shared earlier, indeed, these are some concerns because some of the surveys may touch on issues with regard to security or it may affect market sentiments on specific sectors.

sections.label: Assessing cybersecurity savviness difficulty
sections.summary: Assessing cybersecurity savviness is difficult to measure because technology and products move rapidly and are not thought of today.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: She asked about how we assess the savviness with respect to cybersecurity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: It is a very difficult thing to measure because the technology is moving quite rapidly and the kinds of products and services that are being developed are also not thought of today.

sections.label: Technology versus human behaviour
sections.summary: Technology is easier to measure through penetration testing and audits, but human behaviour is harder to measure, assess and change.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: In a way, technology is the easier thing to measure.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: So, we can do, for example, penetration testing, we can do audits on the use of technology, audits about processes with respect to, for example, thumb drives and locking down systems and Internet surfing separation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
sentences.text: But the much harder thing to measure and assess and change is human behaviour – do not share your passwords, do not download suspicious materials – which is why I took the opportunity to remind Members of these few things that we should do.

sections.label: Act and PDPC complaint resolution
sections.summary: That is provided under the Act, and the PDPC could direct resolution of a complaint as it considers fit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: We know that is provided under the Act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: It is also provided that the PDPC could direct resolution of a complaint in a way that it considers fit.
